topic.title: Neural Robustness, Generalization, and Hidden Vulnerabilities
topic.overview: This topic investigates how neural networks respond to input attacks, damaged connections, altered weights, and malicious training. It combines empirical studies of robust generalization with certificates and impossibility results. The threat model matters: resistance to small input changes is different from detecting a backdoor inserted by the trainer.
topic.whyItMatters: A defense can appear strong on training attacks yet overfit and lose robustness on new examples. Conversely, limits on detecting maliciously trained models show why inspecting weights alone may not establish trust under every adversary.
topic.evolution: The collection includes a 1990 examination of connection damage, followed by constraints-based robustness measures and scalable defenses. Later work exposes robust overfitting and analyzes local geometry. Recent backdoor results examine stronger adversaries and gaps between robust teachers and students. These findings complicate simple claims that sparsity, scale, or longer training automatically improve security.
openQuestions: How can robust evaluation detect training-specific overfitting?
Which trust assumptions remain necessary when model providers themselves may be adversarial?

papers.tldr: The paper formally examines whether neural networks tolerate connection loss and whether efficient computation requires dense connectivity.

papers.tldr: Parseval networks constrain layer sensitivity through approximately Parseval weight matrices, improving adversarial robustness while maintaining strong benchmark accuracy.

papers.tldr: The paper derives and experimentally verifies lower bounds on the perturbation magnitude needed to change a neural network's classification.

papers.title: Differentiable Abstract Interpretation for Provably Robust Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper uses abstract interpretation to train large neural networks with certified robustness while balancing computational efficiency and analysis precision.

papers.title: K-Beam Minimax: Efficient Optimization for Deep Adversarial Learning
papers.tldr: K-Beam tracks multiple inner maximizers to address discontinuities that can derail alternating minimax optimization.

papers.title: Max-Mahalanobis Linear Discriminant Analysis Networks
papers.tldr: MM-LDA shapes learned features around a distribution with a conditional robustness guarantee for its final classifier.

papers.title: Provable Defenses against Adversarial Examples via the Convex Outer Adversarial Polytope

papers.title: The Hidden Vulnerability of Distributed Learning in Byzantium

papers.title: Towards Fast Computation of Certified Robustness for ReLU Networks

papers.title: Efficient Formal Safety Analysis of Neural Networks

papers.title: Efficient Neural Network Robustness Certification with General Activation Functions
papers.tldr: CROWN certifies robustness across general activation functions using adaptive linear and quadratic bounds.

papers.title: Fast and Effective Robustness Certification
papers.tldr: DeepZ uses neural-network-specific abstract interpretation to provide scalable robustness certification that accounts for floating-point arithmetic.

papers.title: Lipschitz-Margin Training: Scalable Certification of Perturbation Invariance for Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Lipschitz-margin calculations and training efficiently certify and enlarge regions of perturbation invariance, including for large networks in experiments.

papers.title: Scaling provable adversarial defenses
papers.tldr: Modular robustness training, random projections, and cascades scale provable defenses and improve certified error bounds on MNIST and CIFAR.

papers.title: Semidefinite relaxations for certifying robustness to adversarial examples
papers.tldr: A tighter semidefinite relaxation provides meaningful robustness certificates for three ReLU networks trained without using that relaxation.

papers.title: Sparse DNNs with Improved Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Appropriate sparsity can improve nonlinear neural-network robustness, but excessive pruning can make adversarial resistance worse.

papers.title: Exploring the Landscape of Spatial Robustness
papers.tldr: Rotations and translations expose classifier weaknesses that require distinct robustness improvements and more reliable attack searches.

papers.title: First-Order Adversarial Vulnerability of Neural Networks and Input Dimension
papers.tldr: Input-gradient scaling links larger input dimensions to greater adversarial vulnerability, with a proof at initialization and supporting observations after training.

papers.title: On the Connection Between Adversarial Robustness and Saliency Map Interpretability
papers.tldr: The paper links decision-boundary distance to saliency alignment exactly for linear models and investigates how neural-network nonlinearity weakens that relationship.

papers.title: On the Convergence and Robustness of Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: Gradually increasing adversarial-example convergence quality improves robustness, reflecting different needs early and late in training.

papers.title: POPQORN: Quantifying Robustness of Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.tldr: POPQORN quantifies certified robustness for recurrent networks, including LSTMs and GRUs, and supports analysis of individual time steps.

papers.title: PROVEN: Verifying Robustness of Neural Networks with a Probabilistic Approach
papers.tldr: PROVEN extends existing robustness verifiers to produce tighter probabilistic certificates under distributionally characterized input perturbations.

papers.title: Sorting Out Lipschitz Function Approximation
papers.tldr: Norm-constrained GroupSort networks preserve gradient norms and universally approximate Lipschitz functions, supporting tighter distance estimates and provable robustness.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness through Local Linearization
papers.tldr: Encouraging locally linear loss surfaces reduces gradient obfuscation and delivers strong measured adversarial robustness with faster training.

papers.title: Approximate Feature Collisions in Neural Nets
papers.tldr: Neural networks can map substantially different inputs to nearly identical features, with experiments finding abundant regions of such collisions.

papers.title: Convergence of Adversarial Training in Overparametrized Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper gives a conditional convergence explanation for adversarial training in overparametrized networks and shows that robust interpolation needs more capacity.

papers.title: Invariance-inducing regularization using worst-case transformations suffices to boost accuracy and spatial robustness
papers.tldr: Regularization that encourages spatial invariance improves robustness, with evidence that suitable transformation settings can also improve standard accuracy.

papers.title: ResNets Ensemble via the Feynman-Kac Formalism to Improve Natural and Robust Accuracies
papers.tldr: A mathematically motivated ensemble of noisy ResNets improves clean-image and IFGSM-attack accuracy on CIFAR10.

papers.title: Robust Attribution Regularization
papers.tldr: Robust optimization objectives train neural networks for more robust Integrated Gradients attributions while revealing remaining optimization challenges.

papers.title: Adversarial Learning Guarantees for Linear Hypotheses and Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper bounds adversarial Rademacher complexity for linear predictors, individual ReLU units, and neural networks with one hidden layer.

papers.title: Efficient Proximal Mapping of the 1-path-norm of Shallow Networks
papers.tldr: The 1-path-norm admits an efficient proximal operator and, with differentiable activations, a tighter network sensitivity bound that motivates robustness applications.

papers.title: Implicit Euler Skip Connections: Enhancing Adversarial Robustness via Numerical Stability
papers.tldr: Skip connections inspired by implicit Euler integration improve adversarial robustness in evaluated ResNets and receive theoretical support.

papers.title: Interpolation between Residual and Non-Residual Networks
papers.tldr: A damped differential-equation model connects residual and non-residual networks and improves reported robustness to noisy and adversarial inputs.

papers.title: Minimally distorted Adversarial Examples with a Fast Adaptive Boundary Attack
papers.tldr: A geometric white-box attack searches efficiently for small class-changing perturbations across three norms and supports evaluation at multiple thresholds.

papers.title: Overfitting in adversarially robust deep learning
papers.tldr: Adversarial training can severely overfit, and early stopping matches many reported algorithmic gains in the paper's empirical study.

papers.title: Second-Order Provable Defenses against Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Curvature bounds enable efficient L2 robustness certificates and a training regularizer that improves certified robust accuracy in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Dynamics of the First-Order Adversaries
papers.tldr: For a two-layer network with quadratic loss, projected gradient ascent finds a local adversarial maximum efficiently with high probability.

papers.title: Towards Understanding the Regularization of Adversarial Robustness on Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Empirical analysis links adversarial robustness to feature smoothing and reduced confidence, helping explain degraded performance on natural examples.

papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating the Tradeoff between Robustness and Accuracy
papers.tldr: Augmentation can harm ordinary accuracy even when a perfect robust predictor exists, while robust self-training can mitigate this trade-off.

papers.title: A Closer Look at Accuracy vs. Robustness
papers.tldr: The paper argues that robustness and accuracy can coexist on benchmark datasets, while current training methods struggle to realize both.

papers.title: Adversarial Training is a Form of Data-dependent Operator Norm Regularization
papers.tldr: A specified norm-based adversarial training procedure is theoretically equivalent to data-dependent operator norm regularization.

papers.title: Biologically Inspired Mechanisms for Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Retina-inspired sampling and multiple receptive-field sizes improve neural-network robustness to small adversarial perturbations in the reported studies.

papers.title: Hold me tight! Influence of discriminative features on deep network boundaries
papers.tldr: Controlled training-data perturbations reveal how discriminative features shape neural decision boundaries and how adversarial training induces invariance.

papers.title: HYDRA: Pruning Adversarially Robust Neural Networks
papers.tldr: HYDRA uses the robust training objective to guide pruning, producing compressed networks with leading benign and robust accuracy in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Most ReLU Networks Suffer from $\ell^2$ Adversarial Perturbations
papers.tldr: For most random ReLU networks with shrinking layer dimensions, most inputs admit small adversarial perturbations discoverable by gradient-based methods.

papers.title: On 1/n neural representation and robustness
papers.tldr: Imposing a covariance-spectrum pattern observed in mouse visual cortex improves adversarial robustness in the artificial networks studied.

papers.title: On the Tightness of Semidefinite Relaxations for Certifying Robustness to Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: A geometric analysis identifies when semidefinite robustness certificates are exact and explains their usual conservatism in deeper networks.

papers.title: Over-parameterized Adversarial Training: An Analysis Overcoming the Curse of Dimensionality
papers.tldr: Under stated assumptions, adversarial training of ReLU networks reaches low robust training loss with polynomial rather than exponential width.

papers.title: Smoothed Geometry for Robust Attribution
papers.tldr: Gradient-smoothness conditions motivate training regularization and retraining-free smoothing that improve attribution robustness in image-model experiments.

papers.title: Understanding and Improving Fast Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: GradAlign addresses catastrophic overfitting in fast adversarial training by encouraging locally aligned gradients.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness Guarantees for Random Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: For random deep networks, classification-boundary distance scales with input magnitude divided by the square root of input dimension.

papers.title: CIFS: Improving Adversarial Robustness of CNNs via Channel-wise Importance-based Feature Selection
papers.tldr: CIFS improves tested CNNs’ adversarial robustness by adjusting channel activations according to their relevance to predictions.

papers.title: Double-Win Quant: Aggressively Winning Robustness of Quantized Deep Neural Networks via Random Precision Training and Inference
papers.tldr: Double-Win Quant randomizes precision during training and inference to exploit poor attack transfer across precisions and improve evaluated robustness and efficiency.

papers.title: Globally-Robust Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Training networks with efficient global Lipschitz bounds enables strong verifiable accuracy and inexpensive online robustness certification.

papers.title: Improving Gradient Regularization using Complex-Valued Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A complex-valued network strengthens gradient regularization, improving reported robustness over comparable real-valued networks and approaching multi-step adversarial training.

papers.title: Learning Deep Neural Networks under Agnostic Corrupted Supervision
papers.tldr: The proposed robust trainer limits corrupted examples’ collective gradient influence across classification and regression.

papers.title: Provable Generalization of SGD-trained Neural Networks of Any Width in the Presence of Adversarial Label Noise
papers.tldr: For specified distribution classes, SGD-trained one-hidden-layer leaky ReLU networks of any width compete with the best halfspace despite adversarial label noise.

papers.title: Robust Learning for Data Poisoning Attacks
papers.tldr: Under a specific separability assumption, SGD-trained two-layer ReLU networks resist data poisoning when width satisfies both lower and distribution-dependent upper bounds.

papers.title: Sparse and Imperceptible Adversarial Attack via a Homotopy Algorithm
papers.tldr: A homotopy attack jointly controls sparsity and perturbation size, achieving successful attacks with fewer altered pixels in reported experiments.

papers.title: Towards Certifying L-infinity Robustness using Neural Networks with L-inf-dist Neurons
papers.tldr: Infinity-distance neurons produce 1-Lipschitz networks whose prediction margins support certified robustness to bounded infinity-norm perturbations.

papers.title: Uniform Convergence, Adversarial Spheres and a Simple Remedy
papers.tldr: In the studied adversarial-spheres setting, output bias and sample size govern a generalization-bound failure, and a suitable bias choice eliminates the phenomenon.

papers.title: Adversarial Examples for k-Nearest Neighbor Classifiers Based on Higher-Order Voronoi Diagrams
papers.tldr: An outward geometric search finds adversarial examples for k-nearest-neighbor classifiers, with scalable approximations producing smaller perturbations than tested baselines.

papers.title: Adversarial Examples in Multi-Layer Random ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: Constant-depth random Gaussian ReLU networks admit small input perturbations with large output effects because their local behavior resembles random linear functions.

papers.title: BulletTrain: Accelerating Robust Neural Network Training via Boundary Example Mining
papers.tldr: BulletTrain focuses robust training on dynamically selected important examples, delivering reported speedups without accuracy loss in the tested settings.

papers.title: Can we have it all? On the Trade-off between Spatial and Adversarial Robustness of Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes a setting-dependent trade-off between spatial and adversarial robustness and proposes a curriculum to improve their balance.

papers.title: Do Wider Neural Networks Really Help Adversarial Robustness?
papers.tldr: Wider networks can become less robust at fixed regularization, motivating an adaptive increase in regularization strength as width grows.

papers.title: Drawing Robust Scratch Tickets: Subnetworks with Inborn Robustness Are Found within Randomly Initialized Networks
papers.tldr: Selected subnetworks within randomly initialized networks exhibit strong adversarial robustness without training their weights.

papers.title: Exploring Architectural Ingredients of Adversarially Robust Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: In adversarially trained networks, how capacity is distributed across width, depth, and stages can matter more than simply adding parameters.

papers.title: Formalizing Generalization and Adversarial Robustness of Neural Networks to Weight Perturbations
papers.tldr: The paper jointly analyzes generalization and class-margin robustness under weight perturbations, then uses that theory to design a training loss.

papers.title: Neural Architecture Dilation for Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Neural architecture dilation seeks to improve adversarial robustness with little computational overhead while maintaining a useful balance with standard accuracy.

papers.title: Neural Population Geometry Reveals the Role of Stochasticity in Robust Perception
papers.tldr: Geometric analysis explains how neural stochasticity can improve visual and auditory adversarial robustness while creating a tradeoff with clean-input performance.

papers.title: RoMA: Robust Model Adaptation for Offline Model-based Optimization
papers.tldr: RoMA combines robust proxy training and candidate-specific adaptation to reduce overestimation during offline input optimization.

papers.title: Shift Invariance Can Reduce Adversarial Robustness
papers.tldr: Theoretical examples and empirical tests show that circular-shift invariance can make classifiers more vulnerable to adversarial perturbations.

papers.title: Stable Neural ODE with Lyapunov-Stable Equilibrium Points for Defending Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: SODEF uses stable neural-ODE equilibria and theoretically motivated regularizers to reduce sensitivity to small adversarial perturbations.

papers.title: A Dynamical System Perspective for Lipschitz Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A dynamical-systems view of residual networks yields 1-Lipschitz architectures and convex-potential layers for provable adversarial defense.

papers.title: Benefits of Overparameterized Convolutional Residual Networks: Function Approximation under Smoothness Constraint
papers.tldr: Large convolutional residual networks can approximate function values while maintaining first-order smoothness, partially explaining benefits of overparameterization.

papers.title: Certifying Out-of-Domain Generalization for Blackbox Functions
papers.tldr: A Hellinger-distance framework certifies performance under bounded distribution shifts for blackbox models and bounded losses at large scale.

papers.title: Measuring Representational Robustness of Neural Networks Through Shared Invariances
papers.tldr: STIR measures representational robustness through the input invariances shared by a network and a chosen reference network.

papers.title: Adversarial Reprogramming Revisited
papers.tldr: Random networks can support adversarial reprogramming under specific conditions, while training can sometimes make it fail.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness is at Odds with Lazy Training
papers.tldr: Overparameterized networks in the lazy-training setting can generalize well and be efficiently learnable while remaining vulnerable to one-step adversarial attacks.

papers.title: Defending Against Adversarial Attacks via Neural Dynamic System
papers.tldr: ASODE uses stability-inspired neural dynamics to reduce nearby adversarial perturbations and reports improved robustness in experiments.

papers.title: Efficient Training of Low-Curvature Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Controlling layer curvature produces networks with more stable gradients and improved adversarial robustness while preserving predictive performance in experiments.

papers.title: Evolution of Neural Tangent Kernels under Benign and Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: An empirical study finds that adversarial training rapidly learns a distinct neural tangent kernel that can itself support robustness.

papers.title: Explicit Tradeoffs between Adversarial and Natural Distributional Robustness
papers.tldr: Theory and experiments show that adversarial training can increase spurious-feature reliance and weaken robustness when those correlations change.

papers.title: Gradient Methods Provably Converge to Non-Robust Networks
papers.tldr: In identified settings, gradient flow favors non-robust depth-two ReLU networks even though robust classifiers exist.

papers.title: Improved techniques for deterministic l2 robustness
papers.tldr: New output layers, pooling constructions, and faster orthogonal convolutions improve accuracy and certified l2 robustness.

papers.title: LOT: Layer-wise Orthogonal Training on Improving l2 Certified Robustness
papers.tldr: LOT efficiently trains Lipschitz-constrained convolutional networks and improves reported certified robustness, with further gains from semi-supervised learning.

papers.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Mixture of Experts
papers.tldr: Sparse mixtures of experts show conditional theoretical and empirical robustness advantages over dense networks with comparable computational cost.

papers.title: Pay attention to your loss : understanding misconceptions about Lipschitz neural networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes classification advantages of 1-Lipschitz networks and shows that loss hyperparameters are crucial to their accuracy–robustness trade-off.

papers.title: Rethinking Lipschitz Neural Networks and Certified Robustness: A Boolean Function Perspective
papers.tldr: Boolean-function analysis reveals expressiveness limits in standard Lipschitz networks and motivates an architecture with better empirical certified robustness.

papers.title: Robust Binary Models by Pruning Randomly-initialized Networks
papers.tldr: Pruning fixed, randomly initialized binary networks produces compact adversarially robust models that outperform robust binary comparisons in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Stability Analysis and Generalization Bounds of Adversarial Training
papers.tldr: Approximate smoothness enables stability bounds for adversarial training and helps explain robust overfitting and stability-promoting training techniques.

papers.title: Towards Practical Control of Singular Values of Convolutional Layers
papers.tldr: A tensor-train representation makes actual convolutional singular values controllable in a hardware-friendly form with a stated small expressivity trade-off.

papers.title: Understanding Robust Learning through the Lens of Representation Similarities
papers.tldr: Layerwise representation comparisons reveal reduced specialization and deeper-layer overfitting in robust networks, offering clues to their behavioral trade-offs.

papers.title: What Can the Neural Tangent Kernel Tell Us About Adversarial Robustness?
papers.tldr: NTK analysis connects adversarial vulnerability and training to kernel-defined features, finding that robust features tend to occupy leading eigenspaces.

papers.title: Why Robust Generalization in Deep Learning is Difficult: Perspective of Expressive Power
papers.tldr: Theoretical bounds reveal an exponential model-size separation between robust training and robust generalization in the studied classification settings.

papers.title: Adversarial Parameter Attack on Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Small parameter changes can leave ordinary accuracy largely intact while substantially weakening a network’s adversarial robustness.

papers.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer ReLU Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.tldr: For two-layer ReLU convolutional networks with label noise, the paper establishes conditions separating benign from harmful overfitting.

papers.title: How Many Perturbations Break This Model? Evaluating Robustness Beyond Adversarial Accuracy
papers.tldr: Adversarial sparsity reveals differences in model vulnerability and defense effectiveness that adversarial accuracy alone can miss.

papers.title: Improving Adversarial Robustness of Deep Equilibrium Models with Explicit Regulations Along the Neural Dynamics
papers.tldr: Regulating intermediate states during equilibrium-model computation substantially improves adversarial robustness in the reported experiments.

papers.title: On the Functional Similarity of Robust and Non-Robust Neural Representations
papers.tldr: Model stitching finds accuracy compatibility between robust and non-robust networks, while robustness compatibility changes substantially with layer depth.

papers.title: Robust Counterfactual Explanations for Neural Networks With Probabilistic Guarantees
papers.tldr: A Stability measure gives probabilistic robustness guarantees for counterfactual explanations under a prediction-based model of model change.

papers.title: Robust One-Class Classification with Signed Distance Function using 1-Lipschitz Neural Networks
papers.tldr: OCSDF learns a geometric normality score with 1-Lipschitz networks, yielding certified robustness bounds and competitive one-class classification results.

papers.title: Robustly Learning a Single Neuron via Sharpness
papers.tldr: An efficient algorithm learns a single neuron under adversarial label noise with a constant-factor squared-error guarantee and milder distributional assumptions.

papers.title: Towards Stable and Efficient Adversarial Training against $l_1$ Bounded Adversarial Attacks
papers.tldr: Fast-EG-l1 avoids coordinate descent to improve the stability and robustness of efficient adversarial training against l1-bounded attacks.

papers.title: Adversarial Examples Exist in Two-Layer ReLU Networks for Low Dimensional Linear Subspaces
papers.tldr: For two-layer ReLU networks trained on a low-dimensional linear subspace, the paper explains vulnerability to orthogonal perturbations and identifies training choices that can improve robustness.

papers.title: Adversarial Training from Mean Field Perspective
papers.tldr: A mean field analysis relates adversarial training dynamics and capacity to network shortcuts, width, and dimensions.

papers.title: Certified Robustness via Dynamic Margin Maximization and Improved Lipschitz Regularization
papers.tldr: A differentiable margin regularizer and improved Lipschitz bounds provide a practical approach to strengthening certified classifier robustness.

papers.title: Connecting Certified and Adversarial Training

papers.title: Enhancing Sharpness-Aware Optimization Through Variance Suppression
papers.tldr: VaSSO stabilizes SAM’s parameter-perturbation adversary through variance suppression, improving reported performance and robustness to label noise.

papers.title: Generalizable Lightweight Proxy for Robust NAS against Diverse Perturbations
papers.tldr: A lightweight initialization-time proxy guides architecture search toward robustness across diverse perturbations with reduced search cost.

papers.title: PAC-Bayesian Spectrally-Normalized Bounds for Adversarially Robust Generalization
papers.tldr: A tighter PAC-Bayesian robust generalization bound removes extra assumptions and mismatch terms present in earlier analyses.

papers.title: Revisiting Adversarial Training for ImageNet: Architectures, Training and Generalization across Threat Models
papers.tldr: Small architecture and training changes substantially improve ImageNet adversarial robustness, with different models leading on trained and unseen attack types.

papers.title: Robust low-rank training via approximate orthonormal constraints
papers.tldr: Approximate orthonormal constraints improve the robustness of low-rank neural-network training.

papers.title: Robustness Guarantees for Adversarially Trained Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A lower-bound attack objective enables convergence guarantees for adversarial training of two-layer networks, with end-to-end results assuming linearly separable data.

papers.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Implicit Bias: Generalization vs. Robustness in ReLU Networks
papers.tldr: For clustered data with weakly correlated means, gradient flow favors two-layer ReLU networks that generalize well but remain adversarially vulnerable.

papers.title: Unlocking Deterministic Robustness Certification on ImageNet
papers.tldr: LiResNet residual blocks and the EMMA loss enable stronger certified robustness and scale fast deterministic guarantees to ImageNet.

papers.title: Wasserstein distributional robustness of neural networks
papers.tldr: Wasserstein distributional threat models generalize pointwise adversarial attacks and support new attack algorithms, accuracy estimates, and out-of-sample guarantees.

papers.title: A Theory of Fault-Tolerant Learning
papers.tldr: A theoretical framework shows how the type and variety of faults determine the data needed to learn fault-tolerant models.

papers.title: Benign Overfitting in Adversarial Training of Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Under stated distributional and perturbation conditions, adversarially trained two-layer networks can fit training data closely while retaining near-optimal robust generalization.

papers.title: Can Implicit Bias Imply Adversarial Robustness?
papers.tldr: For the analyzed setting, polynomial ReLU activations allow gradient-flow training of shallow networks to support both generalization and adversarial robustness.

papers.title: Compositional Curvature Bounds for Deep Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Layer-by-layer curvature bounds support adversarial certificates and provide a differentiable regularizer for improving neural-network robustness.

papers.title: Deep Networks Always Grok and Here is Why
papers.tldr: The paper links delayed generalization and robustness to changes in network geometry and demonstrates grokking in practical image-classification settings.

papers.title: Enhancing Adversarial Robustness in SNNs with Sparse Gradients
papers.tldr: Gradient sparsity regularization improves spiking-network robustness, motivated by a bound connecting gradient sparsity to the random-versus-adversarial performance gap.

papers.title: Et Tu Certifications: Robustness Certificates Yield Better Adversarial Examples
papers.tldr: An attack that uses robustness certificates finds adversarial examples more often and with smaller median perturbations in the reported comparisons.

papers.title: Layer-Aware Analysis of Catastrophic Overfitting: Revealing the Pseudo-Robust Shortcut Dependency
papers.tldr: The paper links catastrophic overfitting to early-layer pseudo-robust shortcuts and introduces layer-aware perturbations that mitigate their formation.

papers.title: Uniformly Stable Algorithms for Adversarial Training and Beyond
papers.tldr: ME-A uses a Moreau-envelope reformulation to achieve uniform stability for weakly convex, non-smooth optimization and mitigate robust overfitting.

papers.title: Achieving Domain-Independent Certified Robustness via Knowledge Continuity
papers.tldr: Knowledge continuity provides robustness guarantees based on learned representations and loss, independent of input modality, norms, and distribution.

papers.title: Certified Robustness for Deep Equilibrium Models via Serialized Random Smoothing
papers.tldr: Serialized Randomized Smoothing reuses prior computation to certify Deep Equilibrium Models up to seven times faster with almost unchanged certified accuracy.

papers.title: Stability and Generalization of Adversarial Training for Shallow Neural Networks with Smooth Activation
papers.tldr: For sufficiently wide two-layer networks with smooth activations, the analysis suggests early stopping controls adversarial-training generalization without data-distribution assumptions.

papers.title: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent toward Collaboration between Layers: A Dynamic Analysis of Multilayer Perceptions
